what_it_does: Simulating a quantum computer on a classical CPU or GPU is extremely expensive: even modest circuits with 30-32 qubits (quantum bits) push existing tools to their limits. This paper presents CAST, a compiler toolchain that translates quantum circuit descriptions into optimized code for multiple hardware targets — both regular CPUs and Nvidia graphics cards. A key technique is 'sparsity-aware gate fusion': when many quantum operations can be proven to leave certain qubits unchanged, those qubits are mathematically eliminated before the heavy computation begins, shrinking the problem. For CPUs the tool uses LLVM (a widely-used code-optimization framework) to exploit data-level parallelism; for GPUs it generates low-level PTX instructions directly.
